newsitem.title: DUBAI: Saudi wants to phase out foreign shipping workers.
newsitem.headline: Saudi wants to phase out foreign shipping workers.

text.p: Saudi Arabia wants to phase out all foreign shipping workers to help find more jobs for nationals, a Saudi newspaper said on Monday.

"In the coming phase, the ministry of communications will focus on the Saudization programme in all sectors of transportation, especially in shipping," the Arab News daily quoted the ministry's undersecretary for transportation affairs Ahmad al-Turki as saying.
Foreigners formed 98 percent of workers in the shipping sector, which accounted for eight percent of the kingdom's total labour force, he added.
Turki said the ministry had asked a local consultancy firm to study means of developing the shipping sector and expanding the "Saudization" programme. He gave no further details.
The kingdom has several ports on the Red Sea and on the Gulf.
Of the 18 million people living in Saudi Arabia, about six million are expatriates. Saudis make up less than seven percent of private sector employees.
Saudi citizens for decades favoured well-paid, half-day managerial jobs in the state sector, but the government can no longer create more public sector jobs to employ them.
